thread:
priya: Noticing weird quota attribution in the console after the telemetry header cleanup. Lots of requests are landing in the "unattributed" bucket. Anyone else?
marco: Yep. Looks like the change that replaced `x-rd-quota-bucket` with `x-rd-quota-scope` rolled out to routing yesterday but SDKs are mixed. Some customers' TS/Go libs still send the old header name.
ellie: The routing layer uses quota scope to select tenant-level bucket vs global fallback. If header missing, it defaults to global low-tier bucket -> explains higher token burn and throttles.
chris: Are we sure it's just a header name mismatch? Telemetry sampling layer also filters on `quota_scope` field now; if missing we drop the sample which makes dashboards look empty for affected tenants.
marco: Repro: curl with `x-rd-quota-bucket: team-A` -> throttle and attr to global. curl with `x-rd-quota-scope: team-A` -> correct tenant quota.
priya: Oof. So two effects: wrong quota routing and dropped telemetry. That's why support sees both throttles and blank dashboards.
ellie: We can do a server-side compatibility patch to accept both header names and map old -> new. Low risk. I can add it to the ingress-middleware and gate it behind `compat.quota_header=true`.
chris: We should also consider SDK-side mitigation: patch Python/TS to emit both headers for one release under an opt-in flag. Go release cadence is slower; many Go users pin versions. Dual-header helps but double-headers may trip WAF rules for some customers. Make it opt-in.
marco: Another ask: telemetry ingestion should backfill missed samples for the last 24h where possible so dashboards don't show a regress. That will be heavy but doable if we limit to affected tenants.
priya: Agreed. Action items: 1) ellie to implement compat shim (ingress) and feature-gate it 2) chris to prepare SDK patches (py/ts immediate dual-header opt-in, go hotfix request) 3) marco to run a targeted backfill for telemetry + mute related alerts for 24h 4) ops will monitor for any WAF/edge complaints during dual-header opt-in flip.
ellie: I'll open the PR and include unit tests + healthchecks. I'll also emit a metric `compat.quota_header.enabled` so Console can annotate graphs.
chris: On SDK UX: add a small `compat` toggle in runtime config and document the migration in client release notes. Recommend we keep the dual-header opt-in for 2 releases then flip to default off and remove old header.
marco: Backfill plan: query raw ingress logs for requests with old header in last 24h, rehydrate samples into telemetry pipeline, and recalc quota burn per tenant. I'll request a short maintenance window.
priya: Who will notify customers? We should coordinate a short note to integrators describing header rename, timeline, and recommended upgrade path. Devex can draft.
ellie: DEVEX: pinged.
devops-bot: rollout started  ingress-middleware/quota-compat v1.4 -> canary (eu-central)
chris: I'll push TS/py patch today and mark the dual-header code behind `enableQuotaCompat` flag. Will open a Go bug and offer a hotfix build for customers on request.
priya: Good. Let's also add a short dashboard annotation explaining "quota header rename in progress" so SRE/support aren't surprised by transient numbers.
marco: I'll mute the quota alerts for tenants we identify during the backfill window. Also we should expand end-to-end tests to include both header names, to avoid regressions.
ellie: PR up in ~1h. Tests included.
priya: Thanks all. After the canary looks good we'll flip the feature-gate and begin notifying customers. Follow-up in #postmortems to finalize deprecation timeline. :thumbsup:
